literal: Non-obtaining it fears; if obtained, separation it fears; unceasing sorrow-having [is] my heart.
translation: My heart fears when it cannot attain him, and fears separation when it does. Thus, it is afflicted with unceasing sorrow.
modern: அவரைப் பெற முடியாதபோது என் நெஞ்சம் அஞ்சுகிறது; அவரைப் பெற்றாலோ மீண்டும் பிரிந்துவிடுவோமோ என்று அஞ்சுகிறது. அதனால் என் நெஞ்சம் நீங்காத துன்பத்தை உடையதாக இருக்கிறது.
explanation: The speaker addresses the constant state of anxiety in her heart regarding her lover. When he is away, the heart fears that it might not attain him again. When he is present, it immediately fears the inevitable future separation. Because it is caught between these two fears, the heart is burdened with endless, unceasing sorrow. The poetic lengthening of vowels (alapeṭai) in words like 'பெறாஅமை' (non-obtaining) and 'அறாஅ' (unceasing) emphasizes the prolonged and continuous nature of her suffering.
